```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(condathis)
# The rattler examples run only where rattlerthis is installed.
has_rattler <- requireNamespace("rattlerthis", quietly = TRUE)
```

## What a Backend Does

Every `condathis` function that touches an environment hands the work to a
*backend*.
The backend solves the package specs, downloads and links the packages,
and activates the environment before a command runs.
`condathis` keeps everything else: the arguments, the checks, the messages,
the results and the condition classes.

Two backends exist today:

* **`"micromamba"`** is built in.
  `condathis` downloads the `micromamba` binary when it first needs it and
  finds no usable copy, and runs it as a separate process.
  Every environment uses it unless you ask for another backend.
* **`"rattler"`** comes from the
  [`rattlerthis`](https://github.com/luciorq/rattlerthis) package.
  It uses [`rattler`](https://github.com/conda/rattler), the Rust library
  behind `pixi`, inside the R process.
  There is no package manager binary to download.

Your code stays the same with either backend.
The `method` argument of the environment functions, and of `run()`,
`run_bin()`, `run_pipeline()` and `run_step()`, picks the backend.
Its default, `"auto"`, picks it for you.

## Installing rattlerthis

`rattlerthis` is not on CRAN.
Install it from [R-universe](https://luciorq.r-universe.dev/rattlerthis):

```{r}
#| label: install-rattlerthis
#| eval: false
install.packages(
  "rattlerthis",
  repos = c("https://luciorq.r-universe.dev", getOption("repos"))
)
```

On Windows and macOS, this installs a binary package for the current and
the previous R release.
On Linux, it builds from source, unless you use the
[Linux binary repository](https://docs.r-universe.dev/install/binaries.html)
that R-universe has for Ubuntu.
A build from source needs a Rust toolchain (`rustc` >= 1.88.0 and `cargo`,
from <https://rustup.rs>).
Linux also needs `pkg-config` and the OpenSSL headers, and Windows needs
Rtools.
The [`rattlerthis` README](https://github.com/luciorq/rattlerthis#installation)
lists the requirements of each platform.

You never call `library(rattlerthis)`.
The package exports no functions: `condathis` loads it when `method`
names `"rattler"`, when rattler environments already exist, and, for a new
environment, when the option `condathis.backend_priority` lists
`"rattler"`.

## Choosing the Backend of a New Environment

Without `method`, a new environment uses `micromamba`:

```{r}
#| label: create-jq-env
create_env("jq", env_name = "jq-env", verbose = "silent")
```

Pass `method = "rattler"` to create one with `rattler` instead:

```{r}
#| label: create-rg-env
#| eval: !expr has_rattler
create_env(
  "ripgrep",
  env_name = "rg-env",
  method = "rattler",
  verbose = "silent"
)
```

`list_envs()` covers every backend.
The `backend` column tells you which one owns each environment:

```{r}
#| label: list-envs
#| eval: !expr has_rattler
list_envs()[, c("backend", "env_name")]
```

## Running Commands

Commands need no `method`.
`"auto"` finds the backend that owns the environment, and that backend
activates it:

```{r}
#| label: run-rg
#| eval: !expr has_rattler
res <- run("rg", "--version", env_name = "rg-env", verbose = "silent")
parse_output(res)[1]
```

Environments of different backends work together.
In this pipeline, `ripgrep` from the rattler environment searches a file
and prints its matches as JSON.
`jq` from the micromamba environment turns the JSON into one line per
match:

```{r}
#| label: pipeline
#| eval: !expr has_rattler
notes_path <- fs::file_temp(pattern = "notes-", ext = "txt")
writeLines(
  con = notes_path,
  text = c(
    "micromamba is the built-in backend.",
    "Environments live in the condathis data directory.",
    "rattler is the backend of rattlerthis."
  )
)

res <- run_pipeline(
  run_step("rg", "--json", "backend", notes_path, env_name = "rg-env"),
  run_step(
    "jq", "-r",
    paste(
      'select(.type == "match")',
      '"\\(.data.line_number): \\(.data.lines.text | rtrimstr("\\n") | rtrimstr("\\r"))"',
      sep = " | "
    ),
    env_name = "jq-env"
  ),
  verbose = "silent"
)

parse_output(res)
```

## One Environment, One Backend

The backend that creates an environment owns it for its whole life.
A call that names another backend for it does not move it:

* Functions that change the environment, such as `install_packages()` and
  `remove_env()`, abort with class `condathis_backend_mismatch`.
* Functions that only read it, such as `run()` and `list_packages()`, warn
  with class `condathis_backend_mismatch_warning` and use the owner.

```{r}
#| label: mismatch
#| eval: !expr has_rattler
#| error: true
install_packages("jq", env_name = "rg-env", method = "micromamba")
```

`create_env()` refuses the name under another backend too, so a name
belongs to one backend at a time.
To move an environment to another backend, remove it, then create it again
with that backend.
Each backend keeps its environments in its own directory.
If the same name still ends up under both, for example in a directory
copied by hand, `"auto"` cannot choose, and the call aborts with class
`condathis_backend_ambiguous_env` until `method` names one of them.

## Making rattler the Default

The option `condathis.backend_priority` sets the order that `"auto"` tries
for a *new* environment.
Its default is `"micromamba"`, so installing `rattlerthis` alone changes
nothing.
To create new environments with `rattler`, and keep `micromamba` as the
fallback, put this in your `.Rprofile`:

```{r}
#| label: priority-option
#| eval: false
options(condathis.backend_priority = c("rattler", "micromamba"))
```

With the option set, `create_env()` uses `rattler` without `method`:

```{r}
#| label: priority-create
#| eval: !expr has_rattler
old_options <- options(condathis.backend_priority = c("rattler", "micromamba"))
create_env("jq", env_name = "jq-rattler-env", verbose = "silent")
options(old_options)

list_envs()[, c("backend", "env_name")]
```

Existing environments keep their owner: `jq-env` stays a micromamba
environment.

## Which Backend to Use

Both backends behave the same wherever they can.
They activate environments the same way, cache the activation, install the
`pip:` sections of environment files, and let one R session at a time
change an environment.
The differences you are most likely to notice:

* **Link scripts.**
  `rattler` never runs the `pre-link`, `post-link` and `pre-unlink`
  scripts of packages.
  `condathis` warns with class `condathis_link_scripts_skipped`, and names
  the packages.
  `micromamba` runs them.
  Both run the `activate.d` scripts.
* **No binary, no command line.**
  `rattler` needs no download of a package manager, and nothing runs as a
  separate process to create an environment.
  For the same reason, `verbose = "cmd"` prints a one-line description, and
  the results of `create_env()` and `install_packages()` have `NA` in
  `cmd` and `pid`.
* **Errors.**
  The classes are `condathis`'s with both backends.
  Under a `rattler` failure, the parent condition has the classes
  `rattlerthis_rattler_<kind>`, such as `rattlerthis_rattler_solve`,
  instead of `micromamba`'s status classes.
* **Disk.**
  The package caches are separate, so a package that both backends use is
  downloaded twice.

The [`rattlerthis` README](https://github.com/luciorq/rattlerthis#differences-from-the-micromamba-backend)
and `?rattlerthis` list every difference.
A simple rule: keep `micromamba` for packages whose link scripts matter.
Try `rattler` when you want no extra binary, or a solver inside R.

## Where the Files Live

`get_install_dir()` reports the data directory of each backend:

```{r}
#| label: install-dirs
#| eval: !expr has_rattler
get_install_dir()
```

The `rattler` backend keeps its environments, its package cache and its
channel metadata in `backend_root_dir("rattler")`, the `rattler` directory
inside the data directory of `condathis`.
The functions that manage files cover every backend:

* `clean_cache()` deletes the package caches of `micromamba` and of
  `rattler`.
* `with_sandbox_dir()` redirects the directories of every backend, so code
  in it leaves nothing behind.

## Writing a Backend

The backend system is open: another package can add its own backend with
`register_backend()`, and users then select it with `method`.
The API is experimental, and it may still change between `0.x` releases.
`?register_backend` describes the functions a backend provides, and how
to register them when the package loads.
[`rattlerthis`](https://github.com/luciorq/rattlerthis) is a complete
example.

## Cleaning Up

```{r}
#| label: cleanup
#| results: hide
remove_env(env_name = "jq-env", verbose = "silent")
if (isTRUE(has_rattler)) {
  remove_env(env_name = "rg-env", verbose = "silent")
  remove_env(env_name = "jq-rattler-env", verbose = "silent")
}
```
